business: San Diego residential moving and delivery company with six employees and ambitions to expand across locations
numbers: Owner reports about $300,000 revenue over the preceding 12 months and 62% profit; residential moves supply about 90% of revenue. Charges $165 hourly for two movers plus $150 for truck and equipment. SEO costs $1,000–$1,200 monthly. Reports 17 Google jobs producing $16,000 and six realtor jobs producing $15,000; a separate spoken claim of over $3,000 per realtor job conflicts with those totals. Existing referral offer discounts jobs above $2,000 by $250. Owner estimates 40% of opportunities are lost over price, has roughly 12,000 agent contacts, and targets $2–$4 million per location within two to three years.
question: The owner attributes slow growth to insufficient leads and wants a route to multiple locations.
diagnosis: Hormozi identifies weak offer differentiation and sales comparisons dominated by hourly price. He favors wealthier customers reached through realtors, calls brokerage partnerships the strongest growth opportunity, and considers the model insufficiently developed for multi-location expansion.
advice: Create premium and standard tiers, presenting premium first. Differentiate through defined mover qualifications, packing, materials, and insurance. Explore a bill ceiling with a 50% estimation buffer and an exception for major onsite discrepancies. Test a 10% same-day surcharge, progressing toward 20%, and keep testing premium prices.

Ask about desired mover qualifications, packing supplies, and valuable possessions before quoting. Explain the package's components and use the standard tier when budget requires it. Over time, develop complete moving packages priced by job.

Give realtor clients a premium upgrade at the standard price. Pursue brokerage leaders in person, use existing realtor relationships for introductions, seek inclusion in client packets, and eventually assign someone to manage partner relationships.

Continue text outreach while testing AI-personalized messages against a generic opener, reviewing generated messages before sending. Find agents on Instagram and test following plus messaging, including 10–20 cold messages daily. He also proposes testing local-number and blue-bubble delivery.

Have foremen explain the crew's review incentive, with a suggested $100 monthly award for the most reviews. Publish before-and-after footage at both locations followed by customer feedback, obtain realtor video testimonials, improve sales tracking, and introduce quality assurance as volume grows.
